## Highlights

Maintenance release on top of
[0.7.0](https://github.com/memblin/tkc-lvlab-py/releases/tag/0.7.0):
a dependency and security refresh, one `createvm` networking fix for
Debian 11, and newer default cloud images.

- **`createvm debian11` names the NIC `enp1s0` (fix).** `createvm`
    labelled every guest interface `eth0`. That is harmless for
    network-config v2 (netplan), where the `ethernets` key is only a
    label and the NIC is selected by MAC. Debian 11 uses network-config
    v1 (ENI), where `name` *is* the device ifupdown brings up — and the
    Debian 11 cloud image's virtio NIC is `enp1s0`. With `eth0` in the
    config, networking depended on cloud-init renaming `enp1s0` to
    `eth0`; when that rename didn't happen, `ifup eth0` found no device.
    v1 images now render `name: enp1s0` (still MAC-matched). v2 images
    are unchanged.

    Manifest-path (`lvlab up`) interfaces take their name from
    `interfaces[].name` in `Lvlab.yml`; a Debian 11 machine there should
    use `enp1s0` for the same reason.

- **Dependency and security refresh.** `uv.lock` regenerated with
    `uv lock --upgrade`, covering Dependabot #164 plus newer transitives:
    `typer` 0.27.2 → 0.27.3 (escapes terminal control characters in
    error messages), `python-gnupg` 0.5.6 → 0.5.7, `pycdlib` 1.20.0 →
    1.22.0, `pylint` 4.0.8 → 4.1.3, `pytest` 9.1.1 → 9.2.0, `zensical`
    0.0.62 → 0.0.73, `pymdown-extensions` 11.0.2 → 12.3, `urllib3`
    2.7.0 → 2.8.0, `pysonar` 1.8.0 → 1.10.0.

    - `black` is pinned to **26.10.1**, not the 26.10.0 Dependabot
        proposed: 26.10.0 carries GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2 (CVE-2026-114134,
        in black's GitHub Action — not used here, but there is no
        reason to ship the affected version). The pin moved in both
        `pyproject.toml` and `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
    - The `tqdm` runtime floor rises from `>=4.66` to `>=4.66.3`,
        excluding the releases affected by GHSA-g7vv-2v7x-gj9p.
    - `pre-commit-hooks` v2.3.0 → v6.0.0 (four majors behind).

    `pip-audit` reports no known vulnerabilities across the resolved
    tree.

- **Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (`ubuntu2604`) added to the built-in catalog.**
    `createvm web01.example.com ubuntu2604` works out of the box, and
    the entry is in `docs/Lvlab.example.yml` to copy into a manifest.
    It tracks `resolute/current/` (network-config v2, first-boot user
    `ubuntu`, `--os-variant ubuntu26.04`). On hosts whose osinfo-db
    predates 26.04, the variant falls back with a warning to
    `ubuntu-current` (or a generic Linux variant) — the guest still
    deploys.

- **Default cloud images refreshed.** `debian12` → bookworm
    `20261026-2643`, `debian11` → bullseye `20260821-2577` (in the
    built-in catalog, `docs/Lvlab.example.yml`, and the smoke manifest).
    Debian 11 LTS ended in August 2026; `20260821-2577` is its final
    build, and the entry will be removed once Debian moves bullseye off
    the live mirror. `fedora44` (1.7) is already current; the
    `latest/` / `current/` entries (debian13, almalinux9/10,
    ubuntu2204/2404) roll upstream automatically.

    Previously downloaded images stay in the cache;
    `lvlab images clean` (dry-run by default) lists the superseded
    builds for removal.

## Breaking changes

None. Raising the `tqdm` floor only excludes vulnerable releases.

## Install / upgrade

```bash
uv tool install --upgrade \
  https://github.com/memblin/tkc-lvlab-py/releases/download/0.8.0/tkc_lvlab-0.8.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

## Supported hosts

Unchanged from 0.7.0 — Debian 12 (3.11), Debian 13 (3.13), AlmaLinux 10
(3.12), Fedora 44 (3.14). See
[`docs-extra/host-validation.md`](https://github.com/memblin/tkc-lvlab-py/blob/0.8.0/docs-extra/host-validation.md)
for the matrix.
